translation_notes: The ASK uses the property path rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf*, so it is not a BGP and m{ } cannot express it: s{ } with both initBindings ($value, $class) moved to term position ({v}, {class_rule}); neither variable is projected (ASK), so the interpolation is the exact equivalent of initBindings.
The original query text has no PREFIX lines (rdflib graphs predefine rdf: and rdfs:); the translation declares the two @prefix explicitly, which s{ } needs for its prologue.
resp.askAnswer: s{ } on a graph is lazy, .execute() forces the rdflib Result, askAnswer is kept as is. bool(s{ ASK ... }(g)) would also work.

The driver stubs self (shape.logger.debug prints, make_v_result returns a tuple) and passes Literal values (debug branch), a depth-2 subclass instance, a depth-0 instance, and neighbours (sibling class, instance of a super-class, non-rdf:type link) that must not match. Mutant: dropping the * of the path -> check FAILS.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: `non_conformant` goes. It became True exactly when a report was appended, so the function now returns `bool(reports), reports`. `found` goes: the branches become `if isinstance(v, Literal): debug` and `elif <ask>: continue`, then one `reports.append(self.make_v_result(...))`, with `rept` inlined. The one-line `sparql_ask` string is inlined into the query call. `.askAnswer` becomes the truth value of the Result, which rdflib documents as the same bool for an ASK. The debug message is unchanged.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `elif s{ ASK { {v} rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf* {class_rule} } }(target_graph):`. The truth test executes the lazy query, so translated.ldpy's `.execute().askAnswer` goes. The m{ } form with an rdflib path, `m{ {v} {rdf:type / (rdfs:subClassOf * "*")} {class_rule} }`, also passes the check, but it has 5 more tokens (124 against 119), so s{ } stays.

No exception to the symmetry rule: outside the RDF line the two files are identical. The Python side keeps SPARQL, because a triples-API path would need RDF and RDFS imports that the fixed header does not have (pySHACL uses its own constants).
header_optimization_notes: Both sides: `from rdflib.term import Literal, URIRef` becomes `from rdflib.term import Literal`, because URIRef is unused. The path uses both @prefix (rdf, rdfs), so they stay.
